title: Credit and Collections Terms — Utility Pass-Through Service Grace Period, Courtesy Waivers and Non-Suspension
content:
These terms govern when a late fee may be charged on a Utility Pass-Through Service statement, how a late fee is waived as a courtesy, and the relation between late fees and service.

## 1. Grace period (in force)

A utility late fee may be charged only after the grace period has ended, counted from the statement due date. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, and the fee may be posted no earlier than the day after the last grace day. The due date is the one the statement carries in the account ledger for that statement month, and the length of the grace period is the schedule's grace period.

| Date (hypothetical: due date 21 March, 5-day grace period) | Grace day | May the fee be posted? |
|---|---|---|
| 22 March | 1 | No |
| 26 March | 5 (last grace day) | No |
| 27 March | day after the last grace day | Yes, from this day on |

## 2. Former fee clause — retired

The former clause "The fee is the schedule's late fee amount, charged once per statement, and only when the statement's unpaid amount at the end of the grace period is at least the late-fee minimum; no late fee is charged on a late fee" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the late fee.

## 3. Courtesy waiver (in force)

A courtesy waiver removes one whole utility late fee, posted as a courtesy waiver credit against that fee. No more than the schedule's number of courtesy waivers may be granted in the trailing 12 months — the 12 calendar months ending on and including the handling date, counting the courtesy waiver credits posted in that span — and a waiver is granted only while the account is active.

| Facts (hypothetical, allowance of 1) | Courtesy waiver |
|---|---|
| Account active; no courtesy waiver credit posted in the trailing 12 months | Available — the whole fee is removed |
| Account active; one courtesy waiver credit posted 7 months ago | Not available — the allowance is used |
| Account final billed; no waiver in the trailing 12 months | Not available — the account is not active |

A courtesy waiver removes a whole fee; it does not remove part of one.

## 4. Service is never suspended

Late fees never lead to suspension of service, because suspension of service for nonpayment is not permitted on any schedule.

superseded_clauses: The fee is late_fee_amount, charged once per statement, and only when the statement's unpaid amount at the end of the grace period (utility_msr_statement_unpaid) is at least late_fee_min_past_due; no late fee is charged on a late fee.
